# Lean CUDA

> Experimental Lean 4 compiler backend. Lowers marked declarations to CUDA device code.
> Nightly binaries are distributed here. Compiler source is private. Not upstream Lean.
> Alpha. Prefer markdown over HTML.

## Start here

1. `agent.md` — fail-closed briefing (identity, routing, kernel shape, install rules)
2. `about.md` — short product facts
3. `docs/index.md` — compile path and attributes
4. `docs/kernels.md` — DeviceM and launch ABI
5. `docs/runtime.md` — concurrency, hardware, alpha limits
6. `agent-install.md` — noninteractive nightly install
7. `install.md` — human install notes

Do not scrape HTML for facts. `index.html` / `docs/*.html` / `install.html` are the
human skin of the same pages.

## Nightly automation (JSON)

- Latest pointer: `releases/v1/latest.json` (`release` is null until a nightly exists)
- Index: `releases/v1/index.json`
- Immutable record: `releases/v1/<release-id>.json`
- Schema: `schema/release-v1.schema.json`
- Contract: https://github.com/ranvier-labs/lean4-cuda-nightly/blob/main/docs/RELEASE_CONTRACT.md

## Rules

1. If `latest.json` has a null `release`, say no public nightly exists and stop.
2. After resolving `latest`, pin the immutable release `id`. Never keep `latest` as the version.
3. Map `uname -m` only: `x86_64` → x86_64, `aarch64`/`arm64` → aarch64. Linux only.
4. Checksum-verified install: download the immutable archive URL, compare SHA-256, extract.
   Never use expiring GitHub Actions artifact URLs.
5. `installation.elanToolchain` is convenient. Current elan does not check this channel's
   SHA-256 sidecar; do not call that path checksum-verified.
6. After install, `lean --features` must contain `CUDA`.
7. Runtime prerequisites: CUDA 13 nvcc, compatible NVIDIA driver, supported GPU.
8. Describe the backend as alpha. Lean owns kernel control flow. C++ is instruction-sized
   shims only (TMA, WGMMA, mbarrier, stmatrix, register redistribution).
9. Do not invent APIs or attributes absent from the markdown pages.

Supported channel: nightly. Supported hosts: Linux x86_64 and Linux AArch64.
